columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Founded by Discovery Channel founder John Hendricks; positioned as an online streaming version of Discovery-style nonfiction.
≈20–23M subscribers worldwide (direct + bundled) across 175+ countries by ~2021–2023, small vs Netflix’s 300M+.
Early growth often via low-priced bundles (e.g. FuboTV, Tata Sky); many bundled subs with low ARPU and light engagement.
Historically ~USD 3/mo or USD 20/year; more recent pricing around ~USD 40/year for ad-free access. Thousands of nonfiction titles.

strengths.title: Focused, science-centric catalog
strengths.detail: Strong destination for documentaries, aligns with knowledge clubs, science fans, and educational viewing.

strengths.title: Ad-free, low-cost subscription
strengths.detail: Relatively low annual price vs big streamers, accessible for documentary enthusiasts.

strengths.title: Global availability and bundling
strengths.detail: Available in 175+ countries and often bundled with other services, increasing reach.

weaknesses.title: Small user base vs mainstream streamers
weaknesses.detail: ~23M subscribers is modest vs Netflix, Disney+, or YouTube; niche appeal limits growth.

weaknesses.title: Heavy reliance on bundled subs and low ARPU
weaknesses.detail: Many subscribers come through bundles and may seldom watch, challenging unit economics.

weaknesses.title: Narrow content focus
weaknesses.detail: Nonfiction only, no major scripted dramas or big entertainment franchises.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. CuriosityStream is factual and documentary streaming service for nonfiction long-form video. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

CuriosityStream is a subscription streaming service focused on non-fiction documentaries and factual series about science, nature, technology, and society. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and CuriosityStream side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On CuriosityStream you can use Long-form video as a first-class product job. You need distribution, search, ads, or a native player at platform scale.

Using Kahana with CuriosityStream

You can use both. CuriosityStream keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep hosting and distribution on CuriosityStream. Put the lectures or series that deserve a shelf into Kahana hubs, ideally via embed, then discuss them in a Club. Reach stays on CuriosityStream; Kahana is where the work is findable after the tab is closed, and where you can grow an audience around it.
